---
name: hgraph
description: The dependency graph — Horizon's vendored hgraph core keeps one file per statement/Lean declaration under <project>/hgraph/; `horizon graph frontier` ranks work and agents attach node-scoped comments and reviews. This is the only DAG engine.
---

Each project may carry an **hgraph**: a plain-files semantic graph under
`<project>/hgraph/` — one Markdown node per blueprint statement and per Lean
declaration, typed edges (`uses` = the hard dependency DAG, `formalizes` =
informal↔formal identity). `horizon graph sync` (run automatically at run boundaries)
reconciles the blueprint + Lean sources into it; your **authored** additions
(comments, reviews, metadata) are never touched by sync. The files are
committed to the workspace ledger like everything else.

Use `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …`; when a workspace has one project,
`-p` is optional. Address nodes by `label:<latex-label>` or
`decl:<lean-fqname>` — raw ids are opaque hashes. Most commands accept `--json`.

## Sync it yourself — and act on the warnings

Don't wait for the run boundary: after you change blueprint statements,
`\uses{}`/`\lean{}` annotations, or Lean declarations, run
`"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> sync` and **read its output**. Sync prints warnings for exactly the defects
you can fix on the spot: `\uses{X} has no blueprint node` (missing/mistyped
label), `\lean{Name} not found in Lean sources` (renamed or unwritten
declaration), stale nodes whose source vanished. Fix what your change caused
before moving on; a warning you deliberately leave (e.g. a forward reference
you'll write next) gets a node comment or a memory item so the next session
knows it's intentional. Sync is idempotent and never touches your authored
comments/reviews/metadata.

## Read

- `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> list --state ready` — nodes whose dependencies are all closed:
  provable *now*. Other states: `closed`, `blocked`, `formalized_open`.
- `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` — the ready nodes ranked by how many downstream nodes a
  proof would unlock. **Use this when picking the next node to prove.**
- `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:thm:foo` — one node: statement, `lean_status`
  (`lean_ok | mathlib_ok | sorry | empty`, derived from scanning the Lean, not
  from `\leanok`), deps, attached comments/reviews.
- `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> ancestors label:thm:foo` — the dependency cone.
- `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> stats` — per-state counts for the project.

## Write — per-node progress lives WITH the node

- **Comment = failure memory / progress note on that node.** When an approach
  fails or you learn something node-specific, record it where the next session
  will look first:
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> add comment label:thm:foo --content "tried simp+ring, fails because …"`
  Agent authorship plus run/session/task provenance are filled from the run
  environment; do not copy the note into the blueprint.
- **Review = a Maths / Lean verdict** (independent axes, `good|bad`):
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> add review label:thm:foo --maths good --lean bad --lean-comment "statement ok; proof has a sorry at the succ case"`
- **Metadata**: `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> modify node label:thm:foo --set status=verified`

Prefer node comments over inbox items for anything scoped to ONE node; use the
inbox (skill: `horizon-inbox`) for cross-node or cross-session coordination.

An edge `source --uses--> target` means *source depends on target*. A node is
"ready" when all of its dependencies are closed; prefer `frontier`, which ranks
ready nodes by what they unlock. The dashboard provides the workspace project
switcher and the chapter-collapsed Graphviz view.

## Relation to the blueprint

The DAG **is** the hgraph — there is no second engine and no parser fallback.
It is generated by resolving the blueprint's `\uses{}`/`\lean{}` annotations
against the real Lean sources, so keeping those annotations correct (skill:
`blueprint-conventions`) is exactly what keeps this graph correct. Unresolved
references surface as `horizon graph sync` warnings and as `dangling` entries — read
the warnings rather than trusting `dangling` alone.

---
name: subagents
description: How the Horizon agent delegates to native subagents for review and upkeep — spawning by name, read-only enforcement, dispatch-time model choice, and the dynamic descriptor roster.
---

Subagents are **your team's workers**: focused helpers you (the team lead) spawn
to divide up review and upkeep while you keep proving. This is delegation
*within* your team and needs no permission — distinct from launching new tasks or
runs for *other* teams, which is off by default (see the `horizon` skill,
"Delegating beyond your team"). The `ground` helper is the fresh-context
checkpoint for workspace-wide strategy and hygiene; it is a subagent, not a
second orchestrator role.

Bundled descriptors and any workspace overrides under
`.archon-horizon/subagents/<name>.md` are merged at the start of every `horizon
run`, then compiled into your engine's **native** subagent format,
workspace-local:

- Claude Code → `.claude/agents/<name>.md`
- Codex → `.codex/agents/<name>.toml`

Use the engine's native roster, or list `.codex/agents/*.toml` for Codex and
`.claude/agents/*.md` for Claude, to see every runnable helper. Do not treat an
empty `.archon-horizon/subagents/` directory as an empty roster: that directory
holds workspace overrides/custom helpers only; built-ins such as `ground`,
`janitor`, and `work-reviewer` still appear in the compiled native directory.
Pick the right helper and scope from those generated descriptions.

## Dispatch

Spawn a subagent **by name** through your engine's own native subagent
mechanism, with a focused directive: the slice/scope (a chapter, a task, a
project) and the project it applies to. Spawn several in parallel when the work
divides cleanly, then wait for and reconcile their reports. Give one subagent
one scoped slice so the workspace scales to many projects.

Delegation is part of the normal workflow, not an exceptional recovery path.
For a session that touches more than one file, more than one proof obligation,
or is expected to run longer than ten minutes, dispatch at least one bounded
review/helper before the final report. On a multi-session task, dispatch
`ground` before the terminal completion claim and `janitor` at the scheduled
hygiene checkpoints. Use the engine's native `spawn_agent`/Task mechanism,
wait for the helper to finish, and reconcile its report in your own result. If
no suitable helper is available, state why delegation was skipped in the report.

## Read-only and write scope

A descriptor's `read_only: true` is compiled to real engine enforcement — Claude
`disallowedTools: [Edit, Write, NotebookEdit]`, Codex `sandbox_mode = "read-only"`
— so a read-only reviewer cannot edit source. Every subagent (read-only or not)
can still file issues/memory and write its report via the `horizon inbox` CLI;
that is how read-only agents act. The descriptor's `write_domain` documents what
a writer is expected to touch (Lean/blueprint/reference source).

## Model and effort — the Horizon agent owns the spend

Descriptors intentionally carry no model, tier, or effort setting. Generated
Claude/Codex descriptors inherit the parent session by default. At dispatch time,
the Horizon agent chooses the native model and reasoning effort for that helper:
use the same model/effort for mathematical review, a lighter capable option for
mechanical search/lint/hygiene, and a vision-capable option for page transcription.
If the engine cannot express a per-call override, inherit the parent and record
the choice in the report rather than hiding a model policy in `config.yaml`.

The same rule applies to a named subagent, a bare Task/Agent spawn, or any
workflow fan-out. Match model and effort to the actual slice, and before a large
fan-out check `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. If headroom is low, commit work in
flight first so an interruption loses nothing.

To add or change a subagent, edit its descriptor under
`.archon-horizon/subagents/` — it recompiles on the next run. Do not rely on a
stale hard-coded roster in this skill.

---
name: lean-check
description: Build and check Lean in this workspace and read the errors — use Lean LSP MCP for fast proof-writing feedback, then run faithful kernel verification with `lake build` / `lake env lean`.
---

## Required proof loop

Load this skill before editing a Lean file. Before the first proof edit, invoke
at least one Lean LSP MCP query for the target (`lean_diagnostic_messages` or
`lean_goal`). After every proof edit, invoke diagnostics or the goal query again
before starting another tactic attempt. Use `lean_multi_attempt`, hover, and
search to investigate candidates instead of repeatedly launching a build.

Do not start iterative proof work with `lake build`: it is a slow, final-boundary
check. Use LSP for the edit loop and reserve `lake build` for the final session
validation (or when a kernel check is specifically needed). When LSP is
unavailable or crashes, record that in the report and use the narrowest fallback,
usually `lake env lean <file>` or a single module, rather than silently skipping
the check.

LSP is sufficient between edits and between separate obligations. Do not run a
module build after every proof or repeat a narrow build immediately before a
configured final build that covers the same files. At the final boundary, run
the configured build once and wait for it. Add an earlier narrow kernel check
only when LSP failed, the change crosses an interface LSP cannot validate, or a
specific elaboration/kernel question must be settled before continuing.

- During proof writing, prefer the Lean LSP MCP server for fast local feedback:
  inspect goals/diagnostics at the edited location before running a full build.
  This is the fastest loop for filling proofs.
- Treat LSP feedback as interactive guidance, not final verification. The
  faithful check is Lean's kernel via the project build: run the configured
  build command, `lake build <Module>`, or `lake env lean <file>` from the
  project root.
- Prefer the project's configured build command when validating a task. Otherwise
  use the narrowest faithful check that covers the changed file/module.
- Re-run after each change and repair failures you introduce.
- Read errors top-down — the first error often causes the cascade. For each,
  note the `file:line`, expected vs actual type, and remaining goal.
- A `sorry` left in place is an open obligation, not a success. Do not hide a
  hard obligation behind a new `sorry` unless a hint explicitly allows it.

## Fast LSP proving loop

The `lean-lsp` MCP server gives sub-second feedback — far faster than a build
(10–30s+). Drive proofs with it, then confirm with the kernel. Key tools:

- `lean_goal(file, line)` — the proof state at a line. Call before writing any
  tactic and after each one. Empty `goals_after` = that step closes the goal.
- `lean_diagnostic_messages(file)` — instant errors/warnings after every edit
  (`[]` = no errors, but *not* proof-complete — confirm with `lean_goal`).
- `lean_multi_attempt(file, line, snippets=[...])` — test 3–5 **single-line,
  indented** candidate tactics at once and see exactly which close the goal and
  why the others fail. The highest-leverage tool for filling a `sorry`.
- `lean_hover_info(file, line, col)` — type/signature/docs at an identifier
  (point at the first char). `lean_file_outline(file)` — declarations + line
  numbers without reading the whole file. `lean_run_code("#eval …")` — quick
  standalone `#check`/`#eval`/`#print`.

Core loop: `lean_goal` (what to prove) → search a premise (see the `leansearch`
skill: `lean_local_search` / `lean_leansearch`) → `lean_multi_attempt` (test
candidates) → edit with the winner → `lean_diagnostic_messages` (confirm) →
kernel-check the module at the end.

## Heavy builds — actually wait for them

Read the WHOLE build output, not just pass/fail: warnings (unused variables,
deprecations, `sorry` notices, unexpected recompiles) are actionable — fix the
ones your change introduced, and record pre-existing/toolchain ones as memory
or an inbox issue rather than scrolling past (see the `horizon` skill,
"Warnings are work").

A cold `lake build` (or one that recompiles Mathlib) can take many minutes. The
most common way a session ends on a wrong conclusion is **not waiting for the
build to finish**:

- Do **not** assume you will be "automatically notified" or "re-invoked" when a
  background build completes — whether that happens depends entirely on the
  mechanism you used. If unsure, run the build in the **foreground** and block on
  it until it exits, then read the exit code.
- If you run it in the background, you MUST actively wait: poll its status/output
  until there is a definitive exit code (a monitor / until-loop, re-reading the
  log), and only then conclude. A background job you started but walked away from
  is *not* done.
- Scope the build to the narrowest faithful check (`lake build <Module>` or
  `lake env lean <file>`) to keep the wait short; reserve the full project build
  for final validation.
- Never write your final report — or `complete` an inbox item, or mark a task
  done — while a build that affects your conclusion is still running. If the
  engine cannot wait long enough, say so explicitly under `## Issues` and leave
  the next action clear, rather than implying the proof checked.
- Before marking a task or roadmap item done/blocked/rejected, add a concise
  closing comment with the exact check command, result, relevant files, and any
  caveat. If a task has `roadmap_refs`, make sure the linked roadmap items end
  with a consistent status and their own sync/closing comment.

## When the LSP dies on big import files

The Lean LSP loads the full environment for the file you open. On a file whose
imports pull in most of Mathlib (a broad `import Mathlib` umbrella, or a module
that transitively imports one), that environment is huge and the LSP server can
run out of memory or time out and die. This is an LSP limitation, **not** a
proof error:

- Do not treat an LSP crash/timeout on such a file as a failure of your proof.
  Fall back to the kernel check: `lake build <Module>` or `lake env lean <file>`,
  which verifies faithfully without holding the whole environment interactively.
- Prefer opening the **narrowest** module in the LSP. Avoid pointing the LSP at
  umbrella/`import Mathlib`-style files just to get feedback; edit and inspect
  the specific module you are proving in instead.
- If the LSP has crashed, restart it (or just proceed with `lake build`) rather
  than repeatedly reopening the same giant file and getting the same crash.

---
name: project-git
description: How git works in an Archon Horizon workspace — one out-of-tree workspace ledger (no per-project repos); read a project's history by pathspec or by a session's commit trailers.
---

Read this before running `git diff`/`git log` on a project.

## The model

- **One out-of-tree workspace ledger.** Archon commits to a single repo whose git
  dir is `.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git` with the workspace **root** as its
  work tree (driven via `--git-dir`/`--work-tree`). `<root>/.git` is deliberately
  untouched — it is reserved for a user repo. The ledger records one commit per
  completed session: `config.yaml`, the session's scoped project files, and
  `.archon-horizon/` shared state; never the binary git dirs under
  `.archon-horizon/vcs/`, locks, or other volatile internals.
- **There are no per-project repositories.** A project directory has no nested
  `.git/`, and there is no `.archon-horizon/vcs/<project>.git`. A project's
  "history" is simply the workspace ledger filtered to that project's path.
- **You record your own work by committing to the ledger** with plain `git` (see
  below). Commit after each independently useful, verified proof/file/tooling
  change, before a long build or delegated review, and before expanding scope.
  A multi-hour implementation session should normally have several commits; one
  commit is appropriate only when the work is genuinely atomic. The message +
  diff is how progress is read, so use a semantic, math-first subject. Provenance
  trailers are added automatically; do not write them.

So a plain `git diff` at the root sees only a user repo (if any), never Archon's.
Drive the out-of-tree workspace ledger explicitly (or use `hgit`).

## Recording your work (committing)

Commits go to the ledger, **not** to `<root>/.git` and **not** via any project
`.git` (there is none). Do **not** `export GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` yourself — that
would redirect `lake` and other tooling. Two equivalent ways to commit:

```bash
# 1) The `hgit` wrapper (on the session env as $HORIZON_GIT) — plain git, ledger-scoped:
"$HORIZON_GIT" add path/to/File.lean
"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
  --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'

# 2) The explicit form (identical effect):
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    add path/to/File.lean
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
    --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'
```

Ordinary git: the ledger's index tracks HEAD, so `add` then `commit` records your
files on top of it. Horizon's own commits stage in a private index and never leave
anything staged in your way.

- **Prefer the pathspec commit** — name the paths on the commit itself:
  `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…" --trailer 'Summary=…' -- path/to/File.lean`
  It records exactly those files, ignores whatever else may be staged, and git
  builds its tree from the **current** HEAD — so it cannot silently revert a
  concurrent session's files the way a commit built on a stale index can.
- Add at least one **`Summary` trailer** explaining the important change, not
  merely repeating the subject. Use one trailer per distinct explanation when
  useful. Its value supports Markdown and LaTeX, so concise mathematical context
  such as `--trailer 'Summary=**Invariant.** Preserves $f(x)=x$ on $A$.'` renders
  directly in the dashboard commit item. Keep each trailer on one line; repeat
  `--trailer 'Summary=…'` for a few separate points.
- Do not wait for the whole task to be complete. A checkpoint commit must build
  or otherwise be internally coherent, but it may explicitly leave the next
  named obligation open.
- Stage **explicit paths** you changed rather than `add -A` — the work tree is the
  whole workspace, so `-A` can sweep in unrelated files.
- `Archon-Run`/`Session`/`Role`/`Task`/`Projects` trailers are stamped for you by a
  hook from the session env; your message stays clean.
- Build artifacts (`.lake`, `*.olean`, …) are excluded automatically, and any
  high-confidence credential is **redacted to `XXXX`** in the staged content (not
  blocked), so a broad add still won't leak a secret into the ledger.
- If the guard reports *"redacted possible secret(s) to XXXX"*, it scrubbed a
  matched credential and let the commit through — **rotate the real credential**,
  and check you didn't stage more than you meant to (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_SECRETS=1`
  skips the scan entirely). A *separate* guard still **blocks** a commit that would
  silently delete tracked files you didn't change (a stale-index clobber); re-seed
  the index (`git read-tree HEAD && git add -- <your files>`) rather than forcing it.

Then verify **in the ledger**, and verify the **paths**, not just the SHA — a bare
`git cat-file` runs against `<root>/.git`, which has not seen your commit yet and will
make a perfectly real SHA look fabricated:

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" ls-tree --name-only HEAD -- path/to/File.lean   # empty ⇒ NOT in HEAD
```

## Concurrent sessions and the clobber guard

Several sessions may commit to the ledger at once. A commit whose index was
seeded from an older HEAD (e.g. `read-tree`, then a concurrent session commits,
then you commit) produces a tree that *lacks* the other session's new files —
plain git would commit it without any error and silently delete their work.
The ledger's `pre-commit` guard now rejects any commit that stages deletions
you did not ask for:

- *"this commit would DELETE N tracked file(s) you did not change"* — your
  index base is stale (or you are committing through a polluted shared index).
  **Do not override.** Re-seed and retry; your own edits are safe in the
  working tree, which concurrent commits never touch:

  ```bash
  "$HORIZON_GIT" read-tree HEAD
  "$HORIZON_GIT" add -- <your files>
  "$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…"          # or just: commit -m "…" -- <your files>
  ```

- Deleting a file **on purpose** (moved/retired): set
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_DELETIONS=1` for that one commit.

At the **end of the session**, re-verify content — not just that HEAD moved —
since a stale-based commit elsewhere could have landed after yours (the guard
blocks new offenders, but belt-and-braces):

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" cat-file -e HEAD:path/to/File.lean && \
"$HORIZON_GIT" show HEAD:path/to/File.lean | diff -q - path/to/File.lean
```

If you were clobbered anyway: `read-tree HEAD`, re-add your files from the
working tree, commit once.

## Reading history / a project's diff

Run from the workspace root:

```bash
GD=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git

git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20                       # whole ledger
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20 -- <project-path>     # one project
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- <project-path>
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- '<project-path>/*.lean'
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. show <sha>
```

Each commit carries provenance trailers — `Archon-Run`, `Archon-Session`,
`Archon-Role`, `Archon-Task`, `Archon-Projects` — so you can map a commit to the
run/session that made it and see what it touched without parsing prose:

```bash
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. \
  log --format='%H %(trailers:key=Archon-Session,valueonly)' -- <project-path>
```

To see what the previous Horizon agent changed, find its session's commit(s) by
the `Archon-Session` trailer and diff each against **its own parent** (what that
commit changed).

## Caveats

- With parallel runs the ledger is one shared branch: commits from several runs
  interleave, and a commit's parent may belong to another run or a dashboard
  publish. Diff a commit against its own parent (what *that* commit changed), not
  across a span of sessions — that would fold in unrelated runs' changes.
- The bundled author identity is `Archon Horizon <archon-horizon@local>`.

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivRepAffChallenge
     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0AtlasFromDivRep
     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# Category-correct ambient contract for the rank-one Picard route
    11	
    12	The rank-one locus lives in degree `genus C`, not in `pic0`. This module installs the concrete
    13	ambient maps that the later open-locus restriction must consume:
    14	
    15	* `abelDivAffTrans` maps the widened degree-`n` divisor functor to `picDegLayerFunctor C n`;
    16	* `abelDivAffSigma` extends a represented slice map to the ambient big-site presheaf;
    17	* `abelDivAffGenusSigma` specializes the map using the canonical genus representation.
    18	
    19	The future public `PicRankOneOpen` must therefore be a subfunctor of
    20	`picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C)`, and `DivRankOneOpen` must be an open of
    21	`divRepAffGenusScheme C`. Its `rankOneAbel` is the restriction of
    22	`abelDivAffGenusSigma`, after applying the corresponding Sigma extension. No placeholder locus,
    23	inverse, representability witness, or endgame theorem is postulated here.
    24	-/
    25	
    26	set_option autoImplicit false
    27	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    28	
    29	universe u
    30	
    31	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
    32	
    33	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    34	
    35	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))} {n : ℕ}
    36	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    37	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    38	
    39	noncomputable section
    40	
    41	variable (C n) in
    42	/-- The widened Abel transformation into the intrinsic degree-`n` Picard layer. -/
    43	def abelDivAffTrans : divFunctorAff C n ⟶ picDegLayerFunctor C (n : ℤ) where
    44	  app T := ↾fun s => ⟨abelDivAff' C n T.unop s, fun K _ _ t => degAt_abelDivAff' s t⟩
    45	  naturality T T' g := by
    46	    ext s
    47	    refine Subtype.ext ?_
    48	    exact (picEtMap_abelDivAff' g.unop s).symm
    49	
    50	@[simp]
    51	lemma abelDivAffTrans_app_coe
    52	    (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) (s : divFamZarAff C n T.unop) :
    53	    ((abelDivAffTrans C n).app T s).1 = abelDivAff' C n T.unop s :=
    54	  rfl
    55	
    56	variable (C n) in
    57	/-- Extend a represented widened Abel map from the slice over `Spec k` to the big site. -/
    58	def abelDivAffSigma {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    59	    (rep : (divFunctorAff C n).RepresentableBy D) :
    60	    yoneda.obj D.left ⟶
    61	      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (n : ℤ)) :=
    62	  rep.toSigmaExtension ≫ Over.sigmaExtensionNat (abelDivAffTrans C n)
    63	
    64	@[simp]
    65	lemma abelDivAffSigma_app_fst {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    66	    (rep : (divFunctorAff C n).RepresentableBy D) (T : Schemeᵒᵖ)
    67	    (x : T.unop ⟶ D.left) :
    68	    ((abelDivAffSigma C n rep).app T x).1 = x ≫ D.hom :=
    69	  rfl
    70	
    71	@[simp]
    72	lemma abelDivAffSigma_app_coe {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    73	    (rep : (divFunctorAff C n).RepresentableBy D) (T : Schemeᵒᵖ)
    74	    (x : T.unop ⟶ D.left) :
    75	    ((abelDivAffSigma C n rep).app T x).2.1 =
    76	      abelDivAff' C n (Over.mk (x ≫ D.hom)) (rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk x rfl)) :=
    77	  rfl
    78	
    79	variable (C) in
    80	/-- The ambient genus-degree Abel map on the canonical represented widened divisor scheme.
    81	
    82	This is the map that the future rank-one divisor open must restrict. It is not itself claimed to
    83	be an open immersion. -/
    84	def abelDivAffGenusSigma :
    85	    yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left ⟶
    86	      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)) :=
    87	  abelDivAffSigma C (genus C) (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C)
    88	
    89	end
    90	
    91	end AlgebraicGeometry

    68	def git(*args: str, check: bool = True) -> str:
    69	    git_dir = os.environ.get("HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR")
    70	    work_tree = os.environ.get("HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE")
    71	    if not git_dir or not work_tree:
    72	        workspace = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
    73	        git_dir = str(workspace / ".archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git")
    74	        work_tree = str(workspace)
    75	    result = subprocess.run(
    76	        ["git", f"--git-dir={git_dir}", f"--work-tree={work_tree}", *args],
    77	        cwd=work_tree,
    78	        check=check,
    79	        text=True,
    80	        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
    81	        stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
    82	    )
    83	    return result.stdout

    86	def module_of(path: str) -> str:

    91	def strip_lean_comments_and_strings(source: str) -> str:
    92	    """Remove lexical regions in which `sorry` and `axiom` are prose."""
    93	    out: list[str] = []
    94	    i = 0
    95	    block_depth = 0
    96	    in_string = False
    97	    while i < len(source):
    98	        pair = source[i : i + 2]
    99	        if block_depth:
   100	            if pair == "/-":
   101	                block_depth += 1
   102	                i += 2
   103	            elif pair == "-/":
   104	                block_depth -= 1
   105	                i += 2
   106	            else:
   107	                out.append("\n" if source[i] == "\n" else " ")
   108	                i += 1
   109	            continue
   110	        if in_string:
   111	            if source[i] == "\\":
   112	                out.extend("  ")
   113	                i += 2
   114	            elif source[i] == '"':
   115	                in_string = False
   116	                out.append(" ")
   117	                i += 1
   118	            else:
   119	                out.append("\n" if source[i] == "\n" else " ")
   120	                i += 1
   121	            continue
   122	        if pair == "/-":
   123	            block_depth = 1
   124	            out.extend("  ")
   125	            i += 2
   126	        elif pair == "--":
   127	            end = source.find("\n", i)
   128	            if end == -1:
   129	                out.extend(" " * (len(source) - i))
   130	                break
   131	            out.extend(" " * (end - i))
   132	            i = end
   133	        elif source[i] == '"':
   134	            in_string = True
   135	            out.append(" ")
   136	            i += 1
   137	        else:
   138	            out.append(source[i])
   139	            i += 1
   140	    return "".join(out)

   143	def identifier_count(source: str, identifier: str) -> int:
   144	    return sum(token == identifier for token in IDENTIFIER_RE.findall(source))

   147	def paths_at(revision: str) -> list[str]:
   148	    paths = git("ls-tree", "-r", "--name-only", revision, "--", PROJECT).splitlines()
   149	    return sorted(
   150	        path
   151	        for path in paths
   152	        if path == ROOT_PATH or (path.startswith(LIB_PREFIX) and path.endswith(".lean"))
   153	    )
   154	
   155	
   156	def sources_at(revision: str, paths: Iterable[str]) -> dict[str, str]:
   157	    return {path: git("show", f"{revision}:{path}") for path in paths}
   158	
   159	
   160	def audit(label: str, requested_revision: str) -> dict[str, object]:
   161	    revision = git("rev-parse", f"{requested_revision}^{{commit}}").strip()
   162	    paths = paths_at(revision)
   163	    sources = sources_at(revision, paths)
   164	    modules = {module_of(path): path for path in paths}
   165	    imports = {
   166	        module: IMPORT_RE.findall(sources[path].split("\nnamespace ", 1)[0])
   167	        for module, path in modules.items()
   168	    }
   169	
   170	    reachable: set[str] = set()
   171	    stack = [ROOT_MODULE]
   172	    while stack:
   173	        module = stack.pop()
   174	        if module in reachable:
   175	            continue
   176	        reachable.add(module)
   177	        stack.extend(dep for dep in imports.get(module, ()) if dep in modules)
   178	
   179	    library_modules = sorted(module for module in modules if module != ROOT_MODULE)
   180	    rooted_modules = sorted(module for module in reachable if module != ROOT_MODULE)
   181	    unrooted_modules = sorted(set(library_modules) - set(rooted_modules))
   182	    rooted_paths = [modules[module] for module in sorted(reachable)]
   183	    cleaned = {path: strip_lean_comments_and_strings(sources[path]) for path in rooted_paths}
   184	
   185	    declared: dict[str, str] = {}
   186	    for path in rooted_paths:
   187	        for name in DECL_RE.findall(cleaned[path]):
   188	            declared.setdefault(name, path)
   189	
   190	    carrier_data: dict[str, object] = {}
   191	    for carrier, implementation_prefix in (
   192	        ("DivFamZar", "DivisorFamilyZar"),
   193	        ("DivFamZarAff", "DivisorFamilyAff"),
   194	    ):
   195	        references = [
   196	            {
   197	                "module": module_of(path),
   198	                "occurrences": identifier_count(cleaned[path], carrier),
   199	            }
   200	            for path in rooted_paths
   201	            if identifier_count(cleaned[path], carrier)
   202	        ]
   203	        consumers = [
   204	            entry
   205	            for entry in references
   206	            if not entry["module"].split(".")[-1].startswith(implementation_prefix)
   207	        ]
   208	        carrier_data[carrier] = {
   209	            "rooted_reference_files": len(references),
   210	            "rooted_reference_occurrences": sum(entry["occurrences"] for entry in references),
   211	            "outside_named_implementation_files": len(consumers),
   212	            "outside_named_implementation_modules": [entry["module"] for entry in consumers],
   213	        }
   214	
   215	    options: dict[str, list[dict[str, str]]] = {
   216	        "maxHeartbeats": [],
   217	        "maxRecDepth": [],
   218	        "maxSynthPendingDepth": [],
   219	    }
   220	    for path in rooted_paths:
   221	        for option, value in OPTION_RE.findall(cleaned[path]):
   222	            options[option].append({"module": module_of(path), "value": value})
   223	
   224	    return {
   225	        "label": label,
   226	        "requested_revision": requested_revision,
   227	        "commit": revision,
   228	        "commit_date": git("show", "-s", "--format=%cI", revision).strip(),
   229	        "library_modules": len(library_modules),
   230	        "rooted_modules": len(rooted_modules),
   231	        "unrooted_modules": len(unrooted_modules),
   232	        "unrooted_module_names": unrooted_modules,
   233	        "lean_lines_total": sum(sources[path].count("\n") + 1 for path in paths),
   234	        "lean_lines_rooted": sum(sources[path].count("\n") + 1 for path in rooted_paths),
   235	        "rooted_sorry_tokens": sum(identifier_count(cleaned[path], "sorry") for path in rooted_paths),
   236	        "rooted_explicit_axiom_declarations": sum(
   237	            len(re.findall(r"^\s*axiom\s+", cleaned[path], re.MULTILINE)) for path in rooted_paths
   238	        ),
   239	        "carrier_references": carrier_data,
   240	        "critical_declarations": {
   241	            name: {"rooted": name in declared, "module": module_of(declared[name]) if name in declared else None}
   242	            for name in CRITICAL_DECLARATIONS
   243	        },
   244	        "proof_budget_overrides": options,
   245	    }
   246	
   247	
   248	def main() -> int:
   249	    if len(sys.argv) < 2 or any("=" not in arg for arg in sys.argv[1:]):
   250	        print(__doc__.strip(), file=sys.stderr)
   251	        return 2
   252	    results = []
   253	    for argument in sys.argv[1:]:
   254	        label, revision = argument.split("=", 1)
   255	        results.append(audit(label, revision))
   256	    json.dump({"schema": 1, "revisions": results}, sys.stdout, indent=2)
   257	    print()
   258	    return 0
   259	
   260	
   261	if __name__ == "__main__":
   262	    raise SystemExit(main())

    74	## Critical root
    75	
    76	`AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0CriticalPath.lean` is imported by the umbrella root. It checks the
    77	three current divisor producers, retains the legacy stop theorem as a comparison input, and roots
    78	the following proof chain for the live arbitrary-affine route:
    79	
    80	1. `not_injective_abelSigmaChartAff_of_divFamZarAff` turns two distinct widened families with equal
    81	   chart value into noninjectivity of `abelSigmaChartAff`, including its structure component.
    82	2. `not_injective_chartValueAff_of_not_injective_chartValue` transports the field-dictionary
    83	   obstruction through the injective old-to-widened vehicle and `chartValueAff_toAff`.
    84	3. `not_isOpenImmersion_abelSigmaChartAff_of_not_injective_chartValueAff` consumes the first lemma
    85	   and the injectivity consequence of a presheaf open immersion.
    86	4. `not_isOpenImmersion_abelSigmaChartAff_of_genus_lt_degree` uses Riemann's inequality and an
    87	   effective replacement to supply the noninjective pair whenever a degree-`n` divisor exists
    88	   after a field extension and `genus C < n`.
    89	
    90	The explicit divisor over the extension field is load-bearing: without a nonempty source, the
    91	empty Abel map could be an open immersion. Every other explicit hypothesis in the main theorem is
    92	used, and the theorem assumes no rational point on the curve. Five geometric and cohomological
    93	`relCurve` instances are derived locally from the standing curve package rather than exposed as
    94	caller obligations. The theorem's public type names the finite map used to obtain the pair, the
    95	actual `divFunctorAff` representation, and the extension-field divisor. It is stronger than the
    96	PDF's positive-genus guard because positivity is unnecessary. It is a rooted terminal stop
    97	condition, not a consumed headline milestone.

   242	    (Algebra.ofId A P.cover.Carrier).restrictScalars k

   713	    (Algebra.ofId P.cover.Carrier L).restrictScalars k

   715	      relCurveMap C P.cover.Carrier L =
   716	        (C ◁ Over.overSpecMap psi).left := by
   717	    refine congrArg
   718	      (fun f : overSpec k L ⟶ overSpec k P.cover.Carrier => (C ◁ f).left) ?_
   719	    exact Over.OverMorphism.ext rfl

   721	      picEtMap C (Over.overSpecMap iota) lam.1 =

   725	      C lam.1 P.cover P.representative P.represents.symm

   732	          (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C P.cover.Carrier L)
   733	            P.datum.cechPicClass)) :=
   734	      (relPicDeg_relPicMk L _).symm

   736	        (relPicMap C (Over.overSpecMap psi)
   737	          (relPicMk C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier)
   738	            P.datum.cechPicClass)) := by
   739	      rw [relPicMap_mk, ← hcurve]
   740	      rfl
   741	    _ = relPicDeg L
   742	        (relPicMap C (Over.overSpecMap psi)
   743	          (P.representative : relPic C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier))) := by
   744	      rw [P.datum_class]
   745	    _ = degAt
   746	        (relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier)
   747	          (P.representative : relPic C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier)))
   748	        (Over.overSpecMap psi) :=
   749	      (degAt_relPicToPicEt
   750	        (P.representative : relPic C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier))
   751	        (Over.overSpecMap psi)).symm
   752	    _ = degAt (picEtMap C (Over.overSpecMap iota) lam.1)
   753	        (Over.overSpecMap psi) := by rw [hpresentation]
   754	    _ = degAt lam.1 (Over.overSpecMap psi ≫ Over.overSpecMap iota) :=
   755	      degAt_picEtMap (Over.overSpecMap iota) lam.1 (Over.overSpecMap psi)

   393	      (y ⊗ₜ (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
   394	        Q ⊗[A] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0)
   395	    (q : PrimeSpectrum (Localization.Away f)) :
   396	    ((1 : q.asIdeal.ResidueField) ⊗ₜ[A] y :
   397	      q.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[A] Q) ≠ 0 := by

   399	    PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap A (Localization.Away f)) q

   401	    intro hf
   402	    refine q.isPrime.ne_top (Ideal.eq_top_of_isUnit_mem q.asIdeal
   403	      (Ideal.mem_comap.mp hf) ?_)

   411	      q.asIdeal.comap (algebraMap A (Localization.Away f)) := rfl

   414	      (Algebra.ofId A (Localization.Away f)) hcom

   416	    (RingHom.surjectiveOnStalks_of_isLocalization (Submonoid.powers f)
   417	      (Localization.Away f)).residueFieldMap_bijective
   418	        p.asIdeal q.asIdeal hcom
   419	  let e : p.asIdeal.ResidueField ≃ₗ[A] q.asIdeal.ResidueField :=
   420	    LinearEquiv.ofBijective rho.toLinearMap hrho

   568	  have hyB : ((1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B]
   569	      (P.h0BaseChange B ((1 : B) ⊗ₜ[P.cover.Carrier] y)) :
   570	      K ⊗[B] Sheaf.HModule (P.datum.baseChange B).sheaf 0) ≠ 0 :=
   571	    P.h0BaseChange_one_tmul_ne_zero B K y hiter
   572	  have hH1 : Subsingleton (datumPair (P.datum.baseChange B)).H1 :=
   573	    P.datumPair_h1_baseChange B
   574	  let yB : Sheaf.HModule (P.datum.baseChange B).sheaf 0 :=
   575	    P.h0BaseChange B ((1 : B) ⊗ₜ[P.cover.Carrier] y)
   576	  change (P.datum.baseChange B).sectionsMapTop K
   577	    (Sheaf.HModule.linearEquiv₀
   578	      (Opens.grothendieckTopology ((relCurve C B : Scheme.{u}) : TopCat))
   579	      isTerminalTop (P.datum.baseChange B).sheaf yB) ≠ 0
   580	  exact sectionsMapTop_ne_zero_of_one_tmul_ne_zero
   581	    (P.datum.baseChange B) hH1 yB hyB
   582	
   583	/-- A rank-one presentation has a tied local-away evaluation generator.
   584	
   585	The rank-one field of `P` makes every residue-field fibre of its `H⁰` module nontrivial.
   586	The projective-module generator lemma therefore supplies a single basic open `D(f)` and
   587	one datum section `y` which stays nonzero on every residue fibre over that open.  The same
   588	`y` is transported to a native global section and its unit-lift through the evaluation
   589	counit; the final conjunct records that counit identity explicitly so the future
   590	`divisorOfRankOne` construction consumes this witness rather than an unrelated section.
   591	-/
   592	theorem exists_baseOpen_evaluation_generator
   593	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   594	    (p : PrimeSpectrum P.cover.Carrier) :
   595	    ∃ f : P.cover.Carrier, f ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
   596	      ∃ y : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0,
   597	        (∀ q : PrimeSpectrum P.cover.Carrier, f ∉ q.asIdeal →
   598	          (y ⊗ₜ (1 : q.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
   599	            Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0 ⊗[P.cover.Carrier]
   600	              q.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0) ∧
   601	        (Scheme.Modules.Hom.app P.evaluation
   602	          ((relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)) ⁻¹ᵁ
   603	            (⊤ : (Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)).Opens))).hom
   604	          (P.evaluationLiftOfH0 y) = P.pushforwardSectionOfH0 y := by
   605	  let Q := Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0
   606	  letI : Module.Finite P.cover.Carrier Q := P.h0_finite
   607	  letI : Module.Projective P.cover.Carrier Q := P.h0_projective
   608	  have hfr : Module.finrank p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   609	      (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[P.cover.Carrier] Q) = 1 := by
   610	    rw [← Module.rankAtStalk_eq]
   611	    exact P.h0_rank_one p
   612	  haveI : Nontrivial (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[P.cover.Carrier] Q) :=
   613	    Module.nontrivial_of_finrank_pos (by rw [hfr]; norm_num)
   614	  haveI : Nontrivial (Q ⊗[P.cover.Carrier] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
   615	    (TensorProduct.comm P.cover.Carrier _ _).toEquiv.symm.nontrivial
   616	  obtain ⟨f, hf, y, hy⟩ :=
   617	    Module.exists_fibrewise_tmul_ne_zero_of_projective p (Q := Q)
   618	      (by infer_instance)
   619	  refine ⟨f, hf, y, ?_, ?_⟩
   620	  · simpa only [Q] using hy
   621	  · exact P.evaluation_evaluationLiftOfH0 y
   622	
   623	/-- The fibrewise-regular local equations cut by a tied local-away datum section.
   624	
   625	The nonvanishing proof is derived by
   626	`sectionsMapTop_datumSectionBaseChange_away_ne_zero`; it is not additional witness data.
   627	Together with `exists_baseOpen_evaluation_generator`, this is the immediate local divisor
   628	consumer on the datum side.  Identifying it with the native evaluation zero locus remains
   629	a separate `O`-module base-change contract. -/
   630	noncomputable def baseOpenDatumSectionLocalEquations
   631	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   632	    [IsNoetherianRing P.cover.Carrier]
   633	    (f : P.cover.Carrier)
   634	    (y : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0)
   635	    (hy : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum P.cover.Carrier, f ∉ p.asIdeal →
   636	      (y ⊗ₜ (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
   637	        Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0 ⊗[P.cover.Carrier]
   638	          p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0) :
   639	    (relCurve C (Localization.Away f)).LocalEquations :=
   640	  P.sectionLocalEquationsOfDatumSectionBaseChange
   641	    (Localization.Away f) y
   642	    (fun q => P.sectionsMapTop_datumSectionBaseChange_away_ne_zero f y hy q)
   643	
   644	/-- The local equations cut by the tied datum section represent its base-changed
   645	cocycle datum. -/
   646	theorem baseOpenDatumSectionLocalEquations_picClass
   647	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   648	    [IsNoetherianRing P.cover.Carrier]
   649	    (f : P.cover.Carrier)
   650	    (y : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0)
   651	    (hy : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum P.cover.Carrier, f ∉ p.asIdeal →
   652	      (y ⊗ₜ (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
   653	        Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0 ⊗[P.cover.Carrier]
   654	          p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0) :
   655	    (P.baseOpenDatumSectionLocalEquations f y hy).picClass =
   656	      (P.datum.baseChange (Localization.Away f)).cechPicClass := by
   657	  unfold baseOpenDatumSectionLocalEquations
   658	  exact P.sectionLocalEquationsOfDatumSectionBaseChange_picClass
   659	    (Localization.Away f) y
   660	    (fun q => P.sectionsMapTop_datumSectionBaseChange_away_ne_zero f y hy q)
   661	
   662	/-! ## Degree of the tied datum -/
   663	
   664	/- The high-priority `relCurve.instOver` used by the section bridge and the degree stack's
   665	base-change `Over` instance have the same structure morphism but different instance keys.
   666	Re-key the standard base-change bundle locally before stating the degree theorem. -/
   667	noncomputable local instance (priority := 20000) rankOneDegreeOver
   668	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
   669	    (relCurve C L).Over (Spec (.of L)) :=
   670	  instOverBaseChange C L
   671	
   672	noncomputable local instance rankOneDegreeSmooth
   673	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
   674	    SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (.of L)) :=
   675	  instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C L
   676	
   677	noncomputable local instance rankOneDegreeIntegral
   678	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
   679	    IsIntegral (relCurve C L) :=
   680	  instIsIntegralBaseChange C L
   681	
   682	noncomputable local instance rankOneDegreeQuasiCompact
   683	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
   684	    QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (.of L)) :=
   685	  instQuasiCompactBaseChange C L
   686	
   687	noncomputable local instance rankOneDegreeFiniteH0
   688	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
   689	    Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 0) :=
   690	  instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange C L
   691	
   692	noncomputable local instance rankOneDegreeFiniteH1
   693	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
   694	    Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 1) :=
   695	  instModuleFiniteHModuleOneBaseChange C L
   696	
   697	/-- The cocycle datum tied to a genus-degree presentation has class degree `genus C`
   698	after every field-valued coefficient extension.
   699	
   700	The proof follows the presentation itself: restrict `lam` to its etale-cover carrier,
   701	identify that class with `representative`, rewrite it as the datum's relative Picard class,
   702	and read the defining degree condition of `lam`. -/
   703	theorem datum_classDeg_baseChange
   704	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   705	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra P.cover.Carrier L]
   706	    [IsScalarTower k P.cover.Carrier L] :
   707	    classDeg L
   708	      (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C P.cover.Carrier L)
   709	        P.datum.cechPicClass) = genus C := by
   710	  let iota : A →ₐ[k] P.cover.Carrier :=
   711	    (Algebra.ofId A P.cover.Carrier).restrictScalars k
   712	  let psi : P.cover.Carrier →ₐ[k] L :=
   713	    (Algebra.ofId P.cover.Carrier L).restrictScalars k
   714	  have hcurve :
   715	      relCurveMap C P.cover.Carrier L =
   716	        (C ◁ Over.overSpecMap psi).left := by
   717	    refine congrArg
   718	      (fun f : overSpec k L ⟶ overSpec k P.cover.Carrier => (C ◁ f).left) ?_

     8	/-!
     9	# Canonical pushforward base change for scheme modules
    10	
    11	For a cartesian square of schemes, `canonicalBaseChangeMap` is the Beck--Chevalley mate
    12	
    13	```text
    14	g^* f_* M --> f'_* (g')^* M.
    15	```
    16	
    17	The two coherence theorems identify its pullback followed by the counit with the pullback of
    18	the original counit.  Invertibility is deliberately not asserted here: it is a property of the
    19	module and square, not part of the construction of the canonical map.
    20	-/
    21	
    22	set_option autoImplicit false
    23	
    24	universe u
    25	
    26	open CategoryTheory Limits
    27	
    28	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    29	
    30	/-- The canonical Beck--Chevalley mate for pushforward along a cartesian square. -/
    31	noncomputable def canonicalBaseChangeMap
    32	    {X X' S S' : Scheme.{u}}
    33	    {f : X ⟶ S} {g : S' ⟶ S} {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ S'}
    34	    (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g) :
    35	    Scheme.Modules.pushforward f ⋙ Scheme.Modules.pullback g ⟶
    36	      Scheme.Modules.pullback g' ⋙ Scheme.Modules.pushforward f' :=
    37	  CategoryTheory.mateEquiv
    38	    (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f)
    39	    (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f')
    40	    (((Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp f' g) ≪≫
    41	      Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr sq.w.symm ≪≫
    42	      (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp g' f).symm).hom)
    43	
    44	/-- Pulling back the canonical mate and evaluating recovers its defining pullback telescope. -/
    45	theorem canonicalBaseChangeMap_pullback_counit
    46	    {X X' S S' : Scheme.{u}}
    47	    {f : X ⟶ S} {g : S' ⟶ S} {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ S'}
    48	    (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g) (M : X.Modules) :
    49	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback f').map ((canonicalBaseChangeMap sq).app M) ≫
    50	        (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f').counit.app
    51	          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g').obj M) =
    52	      ((((Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp f' g) ≪≫
    53	        Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr sq.w.symm ≪≫
    54	        (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp g' f).symm).hom).app
    55	          ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj M)) ≫
    56	        (Scheme.Modules.pullback g').map
    57	          ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f).counit.app M) := by
    58	  rw [canonicalBaseChangeMap]
    59	  exact CategoryTheory.mateEquiv_counit _ _ _ M
    60	
    61	/-- After cancelling the pullback telescope, the base-changed counit is the pulled-back
    62	original counit. -/
    63	theorem canonicalBaseChangeMap_counit_cancel
    64	    {X X' S S' : Scheme.{u}}
    65	    {f : X ⟶ S} {g : S' ⟶ S} {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ S'}
    66	    (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g) (M : X.Modules) :
    67	    ((((Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp f' g) ≪≫
    68	      Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr sq.w.symm ≪≫
    69	      (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp g' f).symm).inv).app
    70	        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj M)) ≫
    71	      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f').map ((canonicalBaseChangeMap sq).app M) ≫
    72	        (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f').counit.app
    73	          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g').obj M)) =
    74	      (Scheme.Modules.pullback g').map
    75	        ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f).counit.app M) := by
    76	  erw [canonicalBaseChangeMap_pullback_counit]
    77	  erw [Iso.inv_hom_id_app_assoc]
    78	  rfl
    79	
    80	end AlgebraicGeometry

     9	/-!
    10	# The presentation locus for the rank-one Abel map
    11	
    12	`PicRankOneOpen` is the functorial locus in the degree-`genus C` Picard layer whose pullback to
    13	every affine test admits a tied `PicRankOneLocalPresentation`.  Quantifying after every affine
    14	pullback makes the condition intrinsic on arbitrary test schemes; stability under further
    15	pullback is exactly `picEtMap_comp`.
    16	
    17	The remaining declarations form the corresponding preimages in the widened divisor functor and
    18	in its canonical representing Yoneda functor, together with the restricted Abel transformations.
    19	These are logical subfunctors only.  In particular, this file does not prove that
    20	`PicRankOneOpen` is represented by an open subscheme, and it reserves `DivRankOneOpen` for the
    21	future actual open subscheme of the divisor representer.
    22	-/
    23	
    24	set_option autoImplicit false
    25	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    26	
    27	universe u
    28	
    29	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
    30	
    31	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    32	
    33	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    34	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    35	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    36	variable (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]
    37	
    38	noncomputable section
    39	
    40	/-- The rank-one presentation locus in the degree-`genus C` Picard layer.
    41	
    42	Membership means that every affine pullback of the input plus class admits a local presentation
    43	tied to that pullback.  This is the correct logical subfunctor underlying the future open Picard
    44	locus; no openness or representability assertion is part of this definition. -/
    45	def PicRankOneOpen :
    46	    Subfunctor (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)) where
    47	  obj T := {lam | ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    48	      (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
    49	    Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi
    50	      ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam))}
    51	  map {T T'} f lam hlam A _ _ t := by
    52	    let F := picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)
    53	    have e : F.map t.op (F.map f lam) = F.map (t ≫ f.unop).op lam := by
    54	      apply Subtype.ext
    55	      exact (picEtMap_comp C f.unop t lam.1).symm
    56	    rw [e]
    57	    exact hlam A (t ≫ f.unop)
    58	
    59	/-- The inverse image of `PicRankOneOpen` under the affine widened Abel transformation.
    60	
    61	This name deliberately records only a presentation-theoretic preimage.  It is not the future
    62	open subscheme `DivRankOneOpen`. -/
    63	def divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff :
    64	    Subfunctor (divFunctorAff C (genus C)) :=
    65	  (PicRankOneOpen pi).preimage (abelDivAffTrans C (genus C))
    66	
    67	/-- The same presentation preimage on the Yoneda functor of the canonical genus divisor
    68	representer. -/
    69	def divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter :
    70	    Subfunctor (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)) :=
    71	  (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).preimage
    72	    (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).toIso.hom
    73	
    74	/-- The affine Abel transformation restricted to the rank-one presentation preimage. -/
    75	def rankOneAbelAff :
    76	    (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).toFunctor ⟶
    77	      (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor :=
    78	  (PicRankOneOpen pi).fromPreimage (abelDivAffTrans C (genus C))
    79	
    80	/-- Restrict the canonical representation isomorphism to the rank-one presentation preimage. -/
    81	def rankOneRepresenterRestriction :
    82	    (divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi).toFunctor ⟶
    83	      (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).toFunctor :=
    84	  (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).fromPreimage
    85	    (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).toIso.hom
    86	
    87	/-- The represented genus Abel map restricted to the rank-one presentation preimage. -/
    88	def rankOneAbelRepresented :
    89	    (divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi).toFunctor ⟶
    90	      (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor :=
    91	  rankOneRepresenterRestriction pi ≫ rankOneAbelAff pi
    92	
    93	end
    94	
    95	end AlgebraicGeometry

     9	/-!

    11	
    12	For a scheme `X` over `Spec k`, this file views an `X.Modules` object as a sheaf of
    13	`k`-modules.  The construction keeps the same section types and restriction maps; only the
    14	scalar action is restricted along `k -> Gamma(X, U)`.  It is the dialect bridge needed to
    15	compare a `Scheme.Modules` line bundle with the fixed-base module sheaves used by the Cech
    16	cohomology engine.
    17	-/

    19	set_option autoImplicit false
    20	
    21	universe u
    22	
    23	open CategoryTheory TopologicalSpace Opposite
    24	
    25	namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme
    26	
    27	variable {k : Type u} [CommRing k]
    28	
    29	/-- The base-ring module structure on sections of a scheme module. -/
    30	@[reducible] noncomputable def moduleKSections
    31	    (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (M : X.left.Modules)
    32	    (U : X.left.Opens) : Module k Γ(M, U) :=
    33	  Module.compHom _ (X.left.overAlgebraMap k U)
    34	
    35	attribute [local instance] moduleKSections
    36	
    37	/-- The native structure-sheaf action, with section-notation binders kept explicit. -/
    38	private noncomputable def smulSection
    39	    (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (M : X.left.Modules)
    40	    (U : X.left.Opens) (r : Γ(X.left, U)) (x : Γ(M, U)) : Γ(M, U) :=
    41	  r • x
    42	
    43	/-- The presheaf underlying a scheme module after restriction of scalars to the base ring. -/
    44	noncomputable def toModuleKPresheafOfModules
    45	    (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (M : X.left.Modules) :
    46	    X.left.Opensᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} k where
    47	  obj U := ModuleCat.of k Γ(M, U.unop)
    48	  map {U V} f := ModuleCat.ofHom
    49	    { toFun := fun x => M.presheaf.map f x
    50	      map_add' := fun x y => map_add _ x y
    51	      map_smul' := fun r x =>
    52	        (Scheme.Modules.map_smul M f.unop (X.left.overAlgebraMap k U.unop r) x).trans
    53	          (congrArg
    54	            (fun (s : Γ(X.left, V.unop)) =>
    55	              smulSection X M V.unop s (M.presheaf.map f x))
    56	            (X.left.overAlgebraMap_apply_res k f r)) }
    57	  map_id U := by
    58	    ext x
    59	    exact congrFun (congrArg (fun (f : M.presheaf.obj U ⟶ M.presheaf.obj U) =>
    60	      (ConcreteCategory.hom f : _ → _)) (M.presheaf.map_id U)) x
    61	  map_comp {U V W} f g := by
    62	    ext x
    63	    exact congrFun (congrArg (fun (h : M.presheaf.obj U ⟶ M.presheaf.obj W) =>
    64	      (ConcreteCategory.hom h : _ → _)) (M.presheaf.map_comp f g)) x
    65	
    66	/-- The restricted presheaf is a sheaf because its underlying additive presheaf is unchanged. -/
    67	lemma toModuleKPresheafOfModules_isSheaf
    68	    (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (M : X.left.Modules) :
    69	    Presheaf.IsSheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.left.toTopCat)
    70	      (toModuleKPresheafOfModules X M) := by
    71	  rw [Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_forget _ _ (CategoryTheory.forget (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
    72	  convert (Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_forget _ _
    73	      (CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u})).mp (Scheme.Modules.isSheaf M) using 1 <;> rfl
    74	
    75	/-- A sheaf of `O_X`-modules, viewed as a sheaf of modules over the base ring. -/
    76	noncomputable def toModuleKSheafOfModules
    77	    (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (M : X.left.Modules) :
    78	    Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k) :=
    79	  ⟨toModuleKPresheafOfModules X M, toModuleKPresheafOfModules_isSheaf X M⟩
    80	
    81	/-- Restriction maps of the base-ring sheaf are definitionally those of the scheme module. -/
    82	lemma toModuleKSheafOfModules_obj_map_apply
    83	    {X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (M : X.left.Modules)
    84	    {V W : X.left.Opens} (h : W ≤ V)
    85	    (x : (toModuleKSheafOfModules X M).obj.obj (op V)) :
    86	    ((toModuleKSheafOfModules X M).obj.map (homOfLE h).op).hom x =
    87	      M.presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op x :=
    88	  rfl

    90	namespace Modules
    91	
    92	variable {X : Scheme.{u}}
    93	
    94	/-- A scheme module which is locally isomorphic to the structure sheaf. -/

   219	/-- The bijection `(M₂ ⟶ N) ≃ (M₁ ⟶ N)` induced by a locally bijective morphism
   220	`f : M₁ ⟶ M₂` of presheaves of modules, when `N` is a sheaf. -/
   221	@[simps]
   222	noncomputable def homEquivOfIsLocallyBijective : (M₂ ⟶ N) ≃ (M₁ ⟶ N) where
   223	  toFun φ := f ≫ φ
   224	  invFun ψ := homMk (((J.W_of_isLocallyBijective
   225	      ((PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf R).map f)).homEquiv _ hN).symm
   226	      ((PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf R).map ψ)) (by
   227	        obtain ⟨φ, hφ⟩ := ((J.W_of_isLocallyBijective
   228	          ((PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf R).map f)).homEquiv _ hN).surjective
   229	          ((PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf R).map ψ)
   230	        simp only [← hφ, Equiv.symm_apply_apply]
   231	        replace hφ : ∀ (Z : Cᵒᵖ) (x : M₁.obj Z), φ.app Z (f.app Z x) = ψ.app Z x :=
   232	          fun Z x ↦ CategoryTheory.congr_fun (congr_app hφ Z) x
   233	        intro X r y
   234	        apply hN.isSeparated _ _
   235	          (Presheaf.imageSieve_mem J ((toPresheaf R).map f) y)
   236	        rintro Y p ⟨x : M₁.obj _, hx : f.app _ x = M₂.map p.op y⟩
   237	        have hφ' : ∀ (z : M₂.obj X), φ.app _ (M₂.map p.op z) =
   238	            N.map p.op (φ.app _ z) := CategoryTheory.congr_fun (φ.naturality p.op)
   239	        change N.map p.op (φ.app X (r • y)) = N.map p.op (r • φ.app X y)
   240	        rw [← hφ', M₂.map_smul, ← hx, ← (f.app _).hom.map_smul, hφ, (ψ.app _).hom.map_smul,
   241	          ← hφ, hx, N.map_smul, hφ'])
   242	  left_inv φ := (toPresheaf _).map_injective
   243	    (((J.W_of_isLocallyBijective
   244	      ((PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf R).map f)).homEquiv _ hN).left_inv
   245	      ((PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf R).map φ))
   246	  right_inv ψ := (toPresheaf _).map_injective
   247	    (((J.W_of_isLocallyBijective
   248	      ((PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf R).map f)).homEquiv _ hN).right_inv
   249	      ((PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf R).map ψ))

      "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 \u2014 the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.\n\nTHE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT\n- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` \u2014 reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.\n- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` \u2014 takes the MOST important open representability item.\n- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` \u2014 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where \"important\" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.\n\nCLAIMING \u2014 do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.\n 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.\n 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.\n 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap \u2014 rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.\n\nYOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body \"\u2026\"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts \u2014 propose to the human instead).\n\nSTANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.\n\nWHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. So the bar is explicit:\n- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.\n- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.\n- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P \u2192 P`.\n- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.\n\nCOMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once. Write risky proofs as explicit `sorry` first, measure, then fill. Stage explicit files, never `add -A`.",
